By the end of this arc, you will have created a reproducible project and loaded a real dataset that we'll use for the rest of the series.

🔵 **Slides:** [Open the Arc 2 Slides →](/arcs/arc_2_slides.html)

## Why Project Management Matters

A consistent project structure means a collaborator — or you, six months from now — can open your folder and immediately understand what goes where, without asking you a single question. This is one piece of what we mean by **[reproducibility](/glossary.qmd#reproducibility)**

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## 🔴 For Browser-Based Students
The folder structure, `renv`, and README steps below require a persistent
filesystem — something a browser sandbox can't provide. Directories created
in webR exist only for this page session and disappear on refresh.

Read through these steps to understand *why* a reproducible project needs
them, but you'll need a local R install (Positron or RStudio) to actually
build and keep a project folder. The dataset-loading steps further down
*do* work live in your browser, since they don't depend on anything
being saved.
:::

## Create an R Project

In Positron: **File → New Folder from Project Template → [R Project](/glossary.qmd#r-project)**, or create a plain folder and open it in Positron as your working directory.

## Build Your Folder Structure

```{r}
#| eval: false
dir.create("raw_data")
dir.create("processed_data")
dir.create("scripts")
dir.create("outputs")
```

| Folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `raw_data/` | Original data. Never edit these files directly. |
| `processed_data/` | Cleaned, transformed versions of your data. |
| `scripts/` | Your code. |
| `outputs/` | Figures, tables, and results. |

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## 🟠 Code Tour — File Naming Conventions
- No spaces — use `_` or `-` instead
- Start timestamped files with an ISO date: `YYYY-MM-DD`
- Be descriptive

**Avoid:**
- ❌ `data analysis.R` (spaces)
- ❌ `data.csv` (not descriptive)
- ❌ `final_FINAL_really_final.R` (version chaos)

**Prefer:**
- ✅ `2024-03-15_survey_analysis.R`
- ✅ `participant_demographics_clean.csv`
- ✅ `README.md`
:::

## Initialize `renv`

[renv](/glossary.qmd#renv) tracks exactly which package versions your project uses, so it runs the same way on any machine, including yours a year from now.

```{r}
#| eval: false
renv::init()
renv::snapshot()
```

This creates:

```
├── .Rprofile
├── renv.lock
└── renv/
    ├── .gitignore
    ├── activate.R
    ├── settings.json
    └── library/
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🟣 Learn More — What's actually inside renv.lock?
```json
{
  "R": { "Version": "4.6.0" },
  "Packages": {
    "dplyr": {
      "Package": "dplyr",
      "Version": "1.1.4",
      "Source": "Repository"
    }
  }
}
```
Every package your project depends on gets pinned to an exact version here. When a collaborator runs `renv::restore()`, R installs these exact versions — not whatever happens to be newest that day. The full `renv` documentation is at [rstudio.github.io/renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/).
:::

## Load the Dataset

We'll use this dataset — real RNA-seq data from a published Shank3 mouse study — for the rest of the series.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# ---- Download once, save locally ----
metadata_url  <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv"
rawcounts_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv"

download.file(metadata_url,  destfile = "raw_data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv")
download.file(rawcounts_url, destfile = "raw_data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv")

metadata  <- read.csv("raw_data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv")
rawcounts <- read.csv("raw_data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv")

# ---- For browser-based students only: uncomment the lines below ----
# metadata  <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv")
# rawcounts <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv")
```

Inspect what you loaded:

```{r}
#| eval: false
head(metadata)
str(metadata)
dim(rawcounts)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## ⚪ About This — Why download-and-save here, but read-from-URL in the Code Tour below?
This isn't an inconsistency — it's intentional. In a real project, raw data should live inside your project folder (`raw_data/`) so your analysis doesn't silently depend on the internet being available every time you run it. If the GitHub repo moves, is renamed, or GitHub has an outage, a project with a local copy still runs. A project that re-fetches a URL every time does not.

Browser-based tools like webR can't save a persistent local copy the way a laptop can, so reading from the URL each time is the necessary workaround for that environment — not the ideal pattern. You're seeing a real technical tradeoff, not a mistake.
:::

🟠 **Code Tour — For browser-based students:** you can still load and inspect the real dataset directly from its source, right here:

```{webr-r}
metadata <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_filtered_metadata.csv")
head(metadata)
```

```{webr-r}
rawcounts <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CWML/ARCS/main/data/GSE113754_GeneLevel_Raw_data.csv")
dim(rawcounts)
```

## Write a **[README](/glossary.qmd#readme)**

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("fs")
library(fs)
fs::dir_tree()
capture.output(fs::dir_tree(), file = "README.txt")
```

Then open `README.txt` and fill in the template:

```
This readme file was generated on [YYYY-MM-DD] by [NAME]

GENERAL INFORMATION

Title of Dataset:

Author/Principal Investigator Information
Name:
ORCID:
Institution:
Address:
Email:

SHARING/ACCESS INFORMATION

This data was retrieved through the GREIN web platform, which
interfaces with the NIH Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) repository.
Link to dataset: https://www.ilincs.org/apps/grein/?gse=GSE113754

DATA & FILE OVERVIEW

raw_data/        — original data (never edited)
processed_data/  — cleaned data
scripts/         — analysis code
outputs/         — figures, tables, results
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🟣 Learn More — README Templates
This project's README is a simplified version of the Cornell Research Data Management README template: [Cornell eCommons README Template](https://ecommons.cornell.edu/entities/publication/6effe964-798e-4c21-aac2-4194709ff230)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## ⚪ About This — The project is the unit of reproducibility
It's tempting to think of a single script as "the analysis." But a script alone can't be reproduced — it depends on data files, package versions, and a folder structure that has to exist for it to run. The **project**, not the script, is what makes your work reproducible: the folders, the `renv.lock`, the raw data, and the code together. If you zipped your project folder and sent it to a stranger, could they run it? That's the real test.
:::

## Why We Did It This Way

- Think about the future as you are forming habits
- Document and automate iteratively
- Give your work collaborative potential

...so reproducibility becomes how you work, not someone else's checklist.
